analysis.summary: Roles caused the trouble. roles.secondary agreed only 79.6% because nothing ranks the candidates when more than two qualify, and every one of the 12 reports hesitated on both roles fields. The causes are an unclear "the game calls it that" (wiki infoboxes, internal names, one side's label), a fallback to assault that suits gunships badly, and an infiltrator role written as a mechanic, which is why the Terror Drone sample says infiltrator while all three coders say anti-armour. Two more fields fail in practice even though the agreement script does not measure them: confidence agrees in only 10 of 18 coder pairs (55.6%), because a wiki copy of an official profile was coded as official by one coder and as wiki by another, and it was never said whether pages of one wiki count as independent. Size (Terror Drone tiny or small; SC2 tank measured medium but named large by example), lineage, flavour affinity and availability all agreed but were hesitated on, each in 5 to 9 reports. I propose: rewrite infiltrator as a job; a five-step primary procedure with a strict meaning of official text; a five-step ranking for secondaries; size bands chosen by example; plain confidence and source-kind rules; mechanical rules for lineage and flavour; and four sample fixes (Terror Drone primary and size, IFV secondaries, Hammer lineage).

proposals.evidence: Terror Drone primary: coders A, B and C all chose anti-armour; the sample says infiltrator (roles.primary 66.7% against the reference). All three RA3 reports hesitated here: 'infiltrator (acts inside enemy units) describes the infest literally, but roles must not be mechanics' (A-ra3, B-ra3, C-ra3). Unclear-rule reports A-ra3 and B-ra3 name the same clash. A and C say the anti-armour requires list naming pattern:infest-vehicle tipped them to anti-armour.
proposals.root_cause: data/vocab/roles.json says roles are 'never its mechanic', but the infiltrator description ('Acts inside enemy units, lines or buildings: sabotage, steal, capture') is a mechanic. It copies the pattern category 'infiltration' (infest, hijack, capture, steal). Meanwhile anti-armour's requires names pattern:infest-vehicle, so the list points both ways.
proposals.target: data/vocab/roles.json term infiltrator (description), plus a new entry in roles.tie_breaks
proposals.change:
Infiltrator description, old -> new: 'Acts inside enemy units, lines or buildings: sabotage, steal, capture.' -> 'Spies, steals or sabotages inside or behind enemy lines: steals vehicles or money, shuts down or spies on buildings, plants charges on structures.'
Add tie-break {terms: [infiltrator, anti-armour, anti-infantry, engineer], rule: 'Ask what the unit does once it gets in. If it destroys what it gets into or onto (an infesting drone, a crew killer), use the anti role for that target. If it takes over enemy buildings, it is an engineer. Infiltrator is left for spying, theft and sabotage.'}
proposals.expected: Terror Drone primary: anti-armour for A, B and C (unchanged); the sample changes from infiltrator to anti-armour (see sample-td-primary). Infiltrator is no longer a candidate secondary for the drone, which removes one of the four options the coders weighed (A-ra3, B-ra3). No other pilot unit used infiltrator.
proposals.side_effects: Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md. data/vocab/faction-flavours.json lists infiltrator among soviet's favoured roles, probably because of the drone. Keep it, or move it to allied (its 'stealth and disguise' theme fits spies); that is a generator choice for Mustafa, not a coding rule. Effect on the 28-game scope: the RA2 and RA3 Terror Drones become anti-armour; GLA hijackers, the RA2 Spy and Black Lotus stay infiltrator; RA engineers who capture buildings are engineer.

proposals.evidence: Coders agree on the primary 100%, but 16 hesitations came from all 12 reports. Hammer: the wiki infobox says 'Main battle tank', while the official profile says 'Anti-Armor Tank', StrategyWiki says 'Anti Tank' and the internal name is AntiVehicle (A, B and C ra3). Riflemen: in-game 'Core Infantry' against the wiki's 'an anti-infantry unit' (A, B and C coh1). Battlefield attack helicopter: the Mi-28's Battlelog line says anti-armour but the AH-1Z's does not, and assault's text ('soaks damage, brawls') fits a fragile flier badly; gaps from A-bf and C-bf asked for close air support. SC2 tank: siege and anti-armour both qualify (A, B and C sc2). Unclear-rule reports: A-bf (is it 'only if' or 'if'?), A-coh1, B-bf, B-coh1, B-ra3, C-bf, C-coh1, C-ra3 (which labels count), A-ra3 (label ranking).
proposals.root_cause: The roles list says 'use anti-X as the primary only if the game gives a bonus against X or calls the unit that; generalists are assault'. It never says which text is 'the game' (wiki infobox, official profile copied on a wiki, StrategyWiki, internal file names, one side's model of a mirrored archetype), whether 'only if' is a gate or a trigger, what wins when siege and anti-X both qualify, or what a fast, fragile generalist is.
proposals.target: schemas/source-unit.schema.json unit.roles.primary description (rebuilds docs/fields.md); data/vocab/roles.json list description; source_rule on roles terms assault and raider; the old tie-break sentences move into roles.tie_breaks
proposals.change:
1) roles.json list description -> 'What the unit is for: its job or the targets it is best against, never how it does it (mechanics are patterns). A card has one primary role and up to two secondary roles. Requires says what a unit needs before it can claim a role. A source unit never claims a role whose requires it fails, and meeting them is not enough on its own: the role's description must fit too. Official text means words the game or its makers wrote: the in-game role line, tooltip or production text, the manual, the official site's unit profile and patch notes. It still counts when read through a wiki page that copies it. A wiki's own infobox, prose or tables, strategy guides and internal file names are not official text. For a unit recorded once for several sides, official text counts only when every side's version carries it. How to pick the primary and secondary roles is under roles in docs/fields.md; the tie-breaks settle close calls.'
2) unit.roles.primary description: 'The unit's main job. Go through these steps and stop at the first one that gives a role. Use only the default kit and sourced facts: never passengers, upgrades, loadout picks or proposal fields. 1. Official role line. If the unit's role line in official text (its designation or one-line description) names one of our roles, use it: anti-tank or anti-vehicle means anti-armour, anti-aircraft means anti-air, artillery means siege, sniper means marksman, recon means scout. Main battle tank, core infantry, multipurpose, general-purpose and combat support name no role. A line that names two roles counts only if the main weapon has a bonus against one of them. Skip a named role whose requires the unit fails. 2. No fighting job. If the unit is unarmed or its only weapon is a tool, use the job of its main button: support, transport, engineer, logistics or infiltrator. 3. Reach. Siege if the main weapon is lobbed or the unit deploys into a mode with a long-range gun. Marksman if the main weapon is a sniper weapon that reaches long or further. 4. Bonus. Anti-armour, anti-air or anti-infantry if the game's own data gives the main weapon extra damage against that target, or the main weapon can hit nothing else. Doing little damage to other targets is not a bonus. 5. Generalist. Raider if the unit is fast or very fast with light or no armour. Otherwise assault.'
3) assault source_rule: 'Primary for generalists that are not fast and lightly armoured (step 5 of roles.primary).' Raider description -> 'Hits and runs, picking off isolated targets: fast flankers, gunships that make attack runs.' Raider source_rule: 'Primary for fast or very fast generalists with light or no armour (step 5 of roles.primary).'
4) tie_breaks: {terms: [disabler, area-denial], rule: 'A disabler acts on units; area denial acts on ground.'} and {terms: [buffer, scout], rule: 'Finding and marking enemies is scout; buffer is for boosting allies.'}
proposals.expected: Hammer: step 1, from the official designation 'Anti-Armor Tank' -> anti-armour (A, B, C and the sample all agree). Terror Drone: step 1, designation 'anti-vehicle drone' -> anti-armour (all, and the fixed sample). IFV: designation 'Multipurpose Combat Support' names no role; steps 2 and 3 do not apply; step 4, the default missiles do about three times the damage to aircraft -> anti-air (all, sample). SC2 tank: in-game description 'artillery' -> siege, and step 3 (deploy mode with a long gun) gives the same (all). Riflemen: 'Core Infantry' names no role; the production text names two roles with no bonus; no bonus data; medium speed -> assault (all). Battlefield helicopter: the Mi-28 line alone does not count for a mirrored archetype; no reach and no bonus data; very fast with light armour -> raider for A, B and C (each changes from assault, settling their shared doubt). Primary agreement stays at 100%.
proposals.side_effects: Depends on the armament group's 'main weapon' rule (decision 2A: the buyer fires it); the helicopter's result does not depend on which weapon that is. Rebuild docs/fields.md and docs/vocabularies.md. Effect on the 28-game scope: games whose data has no bonus lines (CoH1 per-armour tables, DoW1, Battlefield) send unlabelled line units to assault and fast, light ones to raider, which is intended. Games with official role lines (the RA3 profiles, SC2 in-game text, CoH role fields) decide at step 1, so see the registry proposal, which says where each game's role line lives. Mirrored archetypes in Battlefield, Wargame and WiC never decide from one side's text.

proposals.evidence: roles.secondary agreement is 79.6%, below the threshold. IFV: A [support, raider], B [raider, scout], C [anti-infantry, support]; the sample has [support, anti-infantry]. Terror Drone: A [scout, disabler], B [anti-infantry, scout], C [disabler, scout]; the sample has [disabler, scout]. 15 hesitations from all 12 reports, nearly all 'only two slots, nothing ranks them' (A-bf, B-bf, C-bf, A-ra3, B-ra3, C-ra3 twice each, A, B and C sc2, A, B and C coh1). Also: 'nothing says how strong a capability must be' (A-bf, B-bf: anti-air called limited), 'may an upgrade-only or doctrine-only capability justify a role' (C-coh1), and 'a requirement only says when a role is possible, not when it should be claimed' (A-sc2).
proposals.root_cause: unit.roles.secondary has no description; the schema only caps it at two. When three or four roles meet their requires, nothing orders them, and nothing says whether passenger, upgrade or loadout capabilities, or proposal fields such as a proposed radar, count.
proposals.change: Add this description: 'Up to two more jobs. A candidate is any role, other than the primary, whose requires the unit meets and whose description fits a sourced part of the unit. Proposal fields never count (a proposed sensor, mount or seat). Drop any role whose target the official text calls a weak or limited point of the unit. Rank the candidates by what they rest on, and keep the first two: 1. Official text calls the unit by the role's word (a scout, hit-and-run, anti-tank). 2. A button, mode or alternate weapon that every copy has. 3. Its weapons in the primary, secondary and alternate slots. Anti-armour and anti-air need a bonus against that target. Anti-infantry also fits a splash weapon, or small arms that do little to vehicles. Any other role needs one of these weapons to meet its requires. 4. Speed, armour or senses alone. Raider: fast or very fast. Assault: medium or heavier armour and a short- or medium-range main weapon. Scout: long sight, a sensor trait or stealth. 5. Passengers, upgrades, loadout picks (option weapons, the default pick included), doctrines or acquired weapons. Rank these by how many of the options give the role. Ties inside a step follow the order of the roles list. Leave a slot empty rather than fill it with a role that rests on none of these.'
proposals.expected: Terror Drone: step 1, the official profile calls it a scout ('a scout first', 'fast scout') -> scout; step 2, the stasis ray is an alternate weapon on an innate toggle with the root trait -> disabler. That gives [scout, disabler] for A and C; B changes from anti-infantry to disabler; it matches the sample. IFV: step 1, the official 'hit-and-run' -> raider (step 4 gives the same from fast speed); anti-armour is dropped because the official text calls its missiles weak against armour; scout has no official 'recon' and no sourced sensor (the sample's radar is a proposal); step 5, most riders give anti-infantry (Peacekeeper, Tanya, Conscript, Desolator, Imperial Warrior, Shinobi, the snipers) against 3 for anti-armour and 1 for support -> [raider, anti-infantry] for A, B and C; the sample changes (see sample-ifv-secondary). SC2 tank: step 3, the bonus against Armored -> anti-armour, and splash -> anti-infantry -> [anti-armour, anti-infantry] (all). Hammer: step 4, heavy armour and a medium-range cannon -> [assault] (all, sample). Riflemen: step 2, the innate Upgrade to Barracks button builds a structure -> engineer; step 3, rifles -> anti-infantry -> [anti-infantry, engineer] (all). Helicopter: step 3, the splash rockets and cannon -> anti-infantry; radar has a proposal basis and does not count; step 5, the TOW, Hellfire and TV picks give anti-armour (3) against the heat seekers' anti-air (1) -> [anti-infantry, anti-armour] (all). Agreement 100%.
proposals.side_effects: Uses the armament default flag and slot names as they stand. The scout step reads sensors only when their basis is sourced, which the sensors group should keep. Rebuild docs. The agreement script needs no change. Effect on the 28-game scope: passenger-set carriers (RA2 IFV, Battlefield transports) and upgrade-heavy squads (CoH, DoW) rank their conditional roles last; that is intended, because the patterns passenger-sets-weapon and upgrade-in-field carry that variety.

proposals.evidence: B coded the IFV [raider, scout], resting scout on the wiki infobox's 'recon' and on its speed. A-bf and C-bf considered scout because of optional radar picks. The existing sentence 'Damage first is a raider, information first is a scout' did not stop speed alone from counting, because scout's requires accepts speed:>=fast.
proposals.root_cause: Scout's requires list lets any fast unit claim scout, so for a fast unit the raider/scout line rests on judgement alone.
proposals.target: data/vocab/roles.json tie_breaks (replaces the sentence in the list description)
proposals.change: Add tie-break {terms: [raider, scout], rule: 'Damage first is a raider, information first is a scout. Speed alone makes a scout only when official text calls the unit a scout or recon unit. Otherwise scout needs a sourced information part: long sight, a sensor trait, stealth, a mark or a reveal.'} The scout requires list stays as it is (cards still need it).
proposals.expected: IFV: no official 'recon' (only the wiki infobox) and no sourced sensor -> no scout for A, B or C. Terror Drone: the official text calls it a scout -> scout stays (all). Helicopter: radar has a proposal basis -> no scout.
proposals.side_effects: None for the validator. Effect on the 28-game scope: fast units with no sensors become raiders unless their official text calls them scouts.

proposals.evidence: Transport: the IFV is called the main Allied troop carrier but has one seat (gaps A-ra3, B-ra3, C-ra3; unclear B-ra3 'is claiming it anyway as atypical acceptable?', C-ra3). Area denial: a sieged tank holds ground by threat but fails the requires (gap A-sc2; hesitations A, B and C sc2). Marksman: the requires is met by any siege gun though the description does not fit (A-sc2 unclear). Point capture: A-coh1, B-coh1 and C-coh1 asked whether 150% capture supports engineer, infiltrator or logistics (unclear A-coh1, B-coh1). Upgrade-only abilities: the sticky bomb is an ability, so the anti-armour requires fails (A, B and C coh1; unclear B-coh1, C-coh1).
proposals.root_cause: The requires lists say when a role is possible, not when it applies. There is no rule for a carrier with fewer seats than a transport, a gun line that denies ground, long-reach guns that are not snipers, or map-point capture.
proposals.target: data/vocab/roles.json: tie_breaks, and source_rule on the terms transport, siege and marksman
proposals.change: tie_breaks: {terms: [area-denial, siege], rule: 'A gun line that holds ground only by the threat of its fire (a sieged tank) is siege or an anti role. Area denial needs something that stays on the ground: mines, a lingering zone, turrets or fortifications.'}; {terms: [engineer, infiltrator, logistics], rule: 'Capturing map control points is a game-mode rule that all infantry share, so a faster capture rate supports no role. Engineer needs structures or gadgets the unit builds or deploys, or enemy buildings it takes over. Logistics needs resources the unit gathers, carries or earns by its own action. Infiltrator needs spying, theft or sabotage.'}. source_rule transport: 'Needs two or more passenger seats. A carrier with one seat is not a transport, whatever the source calls it; its seat shows in crew.passengers and its carry-passengers or passenger-sets-weapon pattern.' source_rule siege: 'A lobbed weapon, a deploy or siege mode with a long-range gun, or a long-range weapon built to break structures. A long-range missile or cannon alone is not siege.' source_rule marksman: 'Only a precise, mostly single-target weapon, such as a sniper, that reaches long or further. A long-range splash or lobbed gun is siege.' No change to anti-armour's requires: an anti-tank tool fired by an ability button does not earn the role, and an upgrade ranks at step 5 anyway.
proposals.expected: IFV: no transport for anyone (as now; this stops future 'atypical' claims). SC2 tank: no area denial and no marksman; secondaries [anti-armour, anti-infantry] (all). Riflemen: engineer rests on the built barracks, not on capture speed; no infiltrator or logistics; anti-armour from sticky bombs is not claimed (all three already left it out).
proposals.side_effects: Rebuild docs/vocabularies.md. The validator is unchanged (source_rule is text only). Effect on the 28-game scope: CoH units that carry their anti-tank charges as abilities lose anti-armour unless they also have an anti-tank weapon. That is consistent with the cards, whose anti-armour requires also wants a weapon.

proposals.evidence: A, B and C all coded anti-armour; the sample has infiltrator (66.7% against the reference). Under infiltrator-is-a-job and roles-primary-procedure, the official designation 'anti-vehicle drone' decides.
proposals.root_cause: The sample followed the mechanic-shaped infiltrator description, which the coders rejected under 'never its mechanic'.
proposals.change: roles.primary: 'infiltrator' -> 'anti-armour'. roles.secondary: [disabler, scout] -> [scout, disabler] (same set, now in ranking order).
proposals.expected: The sample matches all three coders on the primary, and matches A and C (and B after the ranking rule) on the secondaries. The validator stays OK: anti-armour's requires is met by pattern:infest-vehicle and damage:emp.
proposals.side_effects: Rebuild docs/samples.md if it lists roles. Nothing links role:infiltrator. Flavour scoring for the drone then gives [soviet] alone (see flavour-affinity-rule).

proposals.evidence: The sample's [support, anti-infantry] rests only on passenger weapons; the coders split three ways (A [support, raider], B [raider, scout], C [anti-infantry, support]).
proposals.root_cause: The sample was written before any ranking existed; both of its roles come from riders.
proposals.change: [support, anti-infantry] -> [raider, anti-infantry].
proposals.expected: Matches what A, B and C produce under roles-secondary-ranking. The validator stays OK: raider's requires (speed:>=fast) is met by speed fast.
proposals.side_effects: The memorable line and as_player text can stay as they are (they already describe a fast car whose rider sets the gun).

proposals.evidence: Coders agree 100%, but the Terror Drone differs from the sample (all small against tiny: 66.7% against the reference). 9 hesitations in 9 of 12 reports: the drone (A, B and C ra3: tiny's 'small drones' against small's 'one soldier', and it fills an infantry seat); the SC2 tank (A, B and C sc2: 2.3 Marine widths reads medium, but large's example is tanks); the helicopter (A, B and C bf: does the rotor disc count). Unclear rules: A-bf, C-bf, A-ra3, B-ra3, A-sc2, B-sc2, C-sc2.
proposals.root_cause: data/vocab/sizes.json defines small and medium by soldier widths but large and huge only by examples, and has no aircraft examples. Tiny names both 'dogs' and 'small drones', with no rule for units the game handles like soldiers. Strategy games draw soldiers oversized, so measurements and examples disagree.
proposals.target: data/vocab/sizes.json list description and terms tiny, small, medium, large
proposals.change: List description -> 'Footprint seen from above, which sets the hitbox. Pick the band whose examples name what the unit is; examples win over measurements, because strategy games draw soldiers oversized. Only for a unit no example covers, compare it with the same game's foot soldier. Count the hull, fuselage and wings, not a rotor disc or a gun barrel.' tiny -> 'Clearly smaller than one soldier in its own game: hand-sized or knee-high drones and bots, small animals. Hard to hit, easy to lose sight of. A unit the game handles like a soldier (it fills an infantry seat in a transport, or counts as infantry) is small, however small it looks.' small -> 'One soldier: infantry, power-suit troopers, war dogs, and robots or drones the game handles like a soldier.' medium -> 'About two to three soldier-widths: buggies, cars, light walkers, IFVs, light scout helicopters.' large -> 'Main battle tanks, APCs, assault mechs, attack and transport helicopters, fighter jets.' huge unchanged.
proposals.expected: Terror Drone: it fills an infantry seat in transports -> small for A, B and C; the sample changes (see sample-td-size). SC2 tank: the main battle tank example -> large (all). Attack helicopter: the attack helicopter example, rotor disc not counted -> large (all). Hammer large, IFV medium, Riflemen small: unchanged.
proposals.side_effects: No validator effect: tiny and small are both allowed for drones, unarmoured, micro-bot and rotorcraft, and both count as infantry targets. docs/examples/concept-card.example.json (a tiny hover micro-bot) stays valid. Effect on the 28-game scope: RA2 and RA3 attack dogs become small (they fill transport seats), so 'dogs' leaves tiny's examples. Generals battle drones, SC2 interceptors and Battlefield MAV or EOD bots stay tiny.

proposals.evidence: All three coders chose small; the sample has tiny. The sample's own text says the player version 'gives it a soldier-sized hitbox', and size 'sets the hitbox'.
proposals.root_cause: The sample coded the look, not the footprint the game uses.
proposals.target: data/units/ra3.json ra3.soviet.terror-drone body.size, body.notes, uncertain[body/size], memorable, as_player
proposals.change: body.size 'tiny' -> 'small'. body.notes -> 'A spider-like robot that looks smaller than a soldier. Although it comes from the vehicle factory, the game handles it like infantry: it fills an infantry seat in troop transports, so it is coded small. It heals only at a captured hospital or dry dock or at top veterancy, not from an engineer's medical tent or from repair drones.' uncertain body/size note -> 'Sources call it small or diminutive and no source compares it with a soldier; it is coded small because it fills a soldier's seat in transports.' memorable: 'A tiny, disposable robot' -> 'A small, disposable robot'. as_player: 'drawn tiny, but its hitbox is soldier-sized and outlined' -> 'drawn small and low, with a soldier-sized hitbox outlined'.
proposals.expected: The sample matches A, B and C; body.size agreement against the reference reaches 100%.

proposals.evidence: The agreement script does not measure this field; from the unit files: IFV A high, B medium, C high; Hammer A high, B medium, C high; Terror Drone A high, B medium, C high; SC2 A high, B high, C medium; Battlefield and CoH1 all medium. That is 10 of 18 pairs, or 55.6%. 8 hesitations in 8 of 12 reports (A-bf, A-coh1, B-bf, B-ra3, B-sc2, C-bf, C-coh1, C-sc2). Unclear rules: A-coh1, B-bf, C-coh1 (are pages of one wiki independent?), A-ra3, B-ra3 (does a wiki copy of official text count?).
proposals.root_cause: data/vocab/confidence.json term high ('an official source, or two independent established sources') does not say whether a wiki's copy of an official profile counts as official, whether pages of one site are independent, or whether an official source that backs one side point lifts the whole entry.
proposals.change: high -> 'The facts the entry rests on (tier, cost, speed, armour, main weapon and main mechanic) are stated by official text, or by two independent established sources that agree. Official text read through a faithful copy (a wiki page that reproduces an official profile or manual page and says so) counts as official. Pages of one site count as one source. Two different established wikis are independent unless one gives the other as its source.' medium -> 'Those facts come from one established wiki or database (any number of its pages), not contradicted. An official or second source that backs only a side point, such as one patch-note line, does not raise it to high.' Add to the sources[] guidance (schemas/common.schema.json source description): 'With only three slots, cite an independent second site before a second page of the same site.'
proposals.expected: RA3, all three units: A high (the official copy plus two sites), B high (the official copy), C high (C&C Wiki plus StrategyWiki); the sample is high. SC2: A and B high (Liquipedia plus StarCraft Wiki); C medium (one wiki; its patch-note citation covers only a side point; Liquipedia was blocked). That is correct for C's evidence. Battlefield and CoH1: all medium (one wiki). Agreement goes to 16 of 18 pairs (88.9%); the one remaining difference is source access, not the rule.
proposals.side_effects: scripts/agreement.mjs should measure confidence (ranked), lineage and sources.kind from round 2 on. The SC2 registry note already names Liquipedia's rate limit; round 2 should respect it so that every coder can cite both wikis.

proposals.evidence: A coded the C&C Wiki '/Profile' pages (wiki copies of the official RA3 profiles) as official for all three RA3 units; B coded the same pages as wiki; C did not cite them; the sample uses wiki with the note 'Transcribes EA's official unit profile'. Hesitations: A-ra3 sources[1].kind and B-ra3 sources.kind; unclear rules A-ra3 and B-ra3.
proposals.root_cause: data/vocab/source-kinds.json has no rule for a page that lives on a wiki but reproduces official text. The kind matters because it was the only route to high confidence.
proposals.target: data/vocab/source-kinds.json: tie_breaks, and the descriptions of terms official and wiki
proposals.change: official -> 'Publisher or developer, read on their own site or in the game: manual, official site, patch notes, developer posts, in-game text.' wiki -> 'A large, maintained community wiki for the series. A wiki page that copies official text is still a wiki source; say in its note that it copies official text and where the original was.' Add tie-break {terms: [official, wiki], rule: 'Code the site you actually read. A wiki copy of an official profile or manual page is wiki, with a note naming the original; confidence still counts its text as official.'}
proposals.expected: A's three /Profile citations become wiki with a note, matching B and the sample. Blizzard patch notes stay official (all SC2 coders). Confidence no longer depends on this choice (see confidence-rule).
proposals.side_effects: The copy-check is unaffected (it reads the cited page either way). None for the validator.

proposals.evidence: Coders agree with each other (terror-drone, ifv, riflemen, siege-tank; none for the helicopter and the Hammer), but the sample gives the Hammer 'hammer-tank'. 7 hesitations in 7 of 12 reports (A-bf, A-coh1, A-ra3, A-sc2, B-coh1, B-sc2, C-coh1). Unclear rules: A-coh1 and A-ra3 (no naming rule), C-sc2 (only registry games?).
proposals.root_cause: The lineage description ('Shared id for the same design across games, e.g. terror-drone') does not say which games count, how to name the id, or whether one real-world airframe in two series is a lineage.
proposals.change: -> 'Shared id for the same design in two or more games of data/games.json: a unit with the same name, or one its source calls a direct successor, doing the same job. Use the unit's slug in the earliest such game, for example terror-drone (Red Alert 2 and 3), ifv (Red Alert 2's IFV and Red Alert 3's Multigunner IFV) or riflemen (Company of Heroes 1 to 3). Leave it out when no other registry game has the design. A game outside the registry, or the same real-world vehicle in an unrelated series, does not count.'
proposals.expected: Terror Drone terror-drone, IFV ifv and Riflemen riflemen (all, unchanged). SC2 tank: StarCraft 1 is not in the registry -> left out (A, B and C each drop siege-tank). Helicopter: left out (all). Hammer: RA3 only -> left out (all coders; the sample changes, see sample-hammer-lineage).

SC2's own text calls the siege tank a 'Heavy tank'; the CoH Sherman and Panzer IV are medium tanks; WWII has no main battle tanks; and Generals, TD and RA have light tanks. With no example covering them, those units go to measurement, and the SC2 tank at 2.3 Marine widths reads medium. That is the very split the proposal claims to settle: the analyst's 'large' result relies on the coder calling it a main battle tank. 'Medium tank' and MechWarrior's 'medium mech' also invite reading the weight word as the size. (b) APCs in large and IFVs in medium become binding once examples are decisive. The M113 APC (Wargame, WiC, Broken Arrow) would be large while the bigger Bradley IFV is medium. (c) There is no fallback for games without foot soldiers (SupCom, PA, MechWarrior/BattleTech), where 'compare with the same game's foot soldier' cannot be done. (d) 'Small animals' in tiny against 'war dogs' in small can read both ways for a dog. The scores are deterministic, but scoring 'the main weapon's family' turns a field that agreed 100% into one that depends on the main-weapon field, which agreed 77.8%. On the current files, A has no primary weapon on the helicopter, B's main weapon is the rockets and C's is the cannon, so the result splits between [allied, empire] and [allied]. Scoring any weapon in the primary, secondary or alternate slot removes that dependency. The helicopter then scores allied 3 (autocannon, rotor, rotorcraft) against empire 2 (raider, rotor), giving [allied] for all three. Re-checked: drone soviet 3 or 4 against empire 2, giving [soviet]. Hammer [soviet]. IFV [allied]. SC2 soviet 4 with no faction flavour, giving [soviet]. Riflemen allied from the faction with soviet at 1, giving [allied]. A, B and C each drop soviet here, against their unanimous theme call ('cheap numbers'). That is a Mustafa-level choice to flag. The rule also misses: PS2 VS has two faction flavours ['allied', 'empire']; subfactions with none (cnc3 zocom) have no rule for their parent's flavour; a tie at the top when only one place is left.
